PREPARATION AND ANALYSIS OF AN OSCILLOGRAM DATASET FOR RESEARCH OF SINGLE-PHASE EARTH FAULTS IN CABLE NETWORKS
Ивановский государственный энергетический университет имени В.И. Ленина

Single-phase earth faults (SPEFs) are the predominant type of fault in 6-35 kV networks. Modern digital relay protection devices accumulate vast archives of oscillograms; however, this raw data contains a large number of non-informative records and events of a complex nature. This creates significant obstacles to their use in research and in the development of new protection algorithms.

A multi-stage methodology for forming a target dataset from a large industrial archive (50,765 records), primarily from cable networks, is presented. The methodology includes automated primary selection of oscillograms with signs of SPEF using a Python algorithm and subsequent manual expert verification to filter out false positives and refine the labeling.

As a result of the work, a reference set of 795 oscillograms, reliably reflecting the processes during SPEFs, was formed and verified from the initial array. The analysis revealed and systematized a number of characteristic phenomena (measuring circuit limitations, developing faults, switching processes) that significantly complicate the automatic interpretation of oscillograms.

The created verified dataset is a valuable basis for further statistical research. The work emphasizes the necessity of the expert verification stage when working with real data and demonstrates the key problems that must be taken into account when developing intelligent systems for analyzing emergency modes.
